fit: randomized human blend and epigastric pain item
assessment: The 28-day ginger–artichoke blend favored lower epigastric pain trajectory versus placebo (−0.173 transformed units; 95% CI −0.281 to −0.065). It does not isolate ginger or represent Parkinson pain or grated rhizome.
The 2003 artichoke-only trial has a clear global dyspepsia contrast but an imprecise pain item (p=.1786). It cannot isolate the contributions of the different constituents to the 2015 blend.

fit: randomized ginger capsule exposure and endpoint distinction
assessment: In 11 functional-dyspepsia adults, the acute ginger capsules shortened ultrasound half-emptying time but did not clearly change reported stomach sensations. No measured Parkinson pain, colonic transit or constipation effect.
